arguments.text: Bug #4 fixed. Root cause: `isInDST` compared the current offset against the offset of the *same day-of-month* in January and May; in 1974 US DST ran Jan 6 → Oct 27, so for any day ≥ 6 the January reference was itself in DST and the comparison always failed. Anchored both references to `day: 1` (src/datetime.js). Verified: 1974-01-06/06-15/10-26 in America/New_York now report true, 1974-01-05 and 1974-10-27 false, and 2018 New York / Sydney / fixed-offset cases unchanged. It now strips the sign, pads the magnitude and re-prefixes it, so `toISODate()` gives `-0050-01-01`, `-0001-01-01` etc. while positive years and long values are unchanged. import zlib, glob, os, hashlib, subprocess
seen={}
for f in sorted(glob.glob('/tmp/.sb/snap/objects/*/*')):
    try:
        data = zlib.decompress(open(f,'rb').read())
    except Exception:
        continue
    txt = data.decode('utf-8','replace')
    # identify by first import/export signature
    name=None
    for cand in ['src/impl/util.js','src/datetime.js','src/duration.js','src/interval.js','src/impl/conversions.js','src/impl/regexParser.js','src/impl/tokenParser.js','src/impl/formatter.js','src/impl/locale.js']:

        if ('export function objToLocalTS' in txt and base=='util.js') or \
           ('export default class DateTime' in txt and base=='datetime.js') or \
           ('export default class Duration' in txt and base=='duration.js') or \
           ('export default class Interval' in txt and base=='interval.js') or \
           ('export function gregorianToWeek' in txt and base=='conversions.js'):
            name=cand
            break
    if name:
        h=hashlib.md5(data).hexdigest()[:8]
        key=(name,h)
        if key in seen: continue
        seen[key]=f
        cur=open('/luxon/'+name,'rb').read()
        same = (cur==data)
        print(name, h, "len",len(data), "SAME" if same else "DIFF")
EOF

arguments.text: Bug #8 fixed. Root cause: `FixedOffsetZone#isValid` was hard-coded to `true`, so a non-numeric offset produced a "valid" zone with a NaN offset. It now returns `isNumber(this.fixed) && !Number.isNaN(this.fixed)`. Verified: `FixedOffsetZone.instance("blorp"|NaN|undefined|null|{})` is invalid, and DateTimes built via `fromObject({zone})`, `setZone`, `fromMillis/fromSeconds/fromJSDate/fromISO/fromFormat/fromRFC2822` with such a zone are invalid with reason "unsupported zone"; numeric offsets (0, 3, -5, 5.5, UTC+6 specifiers) unchanged. Jest: 892 passed / 2 pre-existing unrelated toFormat failures, identical to baseline; zones suite 32/32 green.
